newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse edges up on higher VSZ average price.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse edges up on higher VSZ average price.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mixed in quiet trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday as uncertainty related to failed referendums last weekend resulted in low activity among foreign investors.
"All (foreign) investors ask about the current political situation and the political risk for their investment." Bohus Betko of ING Barings said.

Trading on the BSE is expected to remain sluggish in coming days as foreign investors will wait until political uncertainty, related mainly to unsuccessful referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections, settle down.
"You can hardly expect investors to come to a country which seems politicaly unstable and where a highly illiquid stock market gives little chances to take the invested funds out," Betko added.
VSZ dominated trading on the BSE main listed floor with 10,286 shares matched, but brokers said the volume appeared only as a settlement of a previously agreed deal at 750 crowns per a share.

VSZ closed down 30 crown at 700, but its average price -- used for calculating the index -- firmed by 2.6 percent which brokers said accounted for the largest part of the SAX index's increase of 2.17 points to 197.69.
"We expect VSZ's price to decline in the near future as the dividend is being gradually deducted from the market price," said Betko. VSZ has approved a 40 crown net crown dividend per a share.
Betko added interest in VSZ share was waning as investors seemed waiting for further declines in its price to buy the stocks cheaper. "The share seems to be heading under 700 crowns," he said.
Overall volume rose to 452,445 stocks, boosted by 441,056 shares matched as direct trades, from 89,956 stocks on Friday. The turnover decreased to 81.45 million crowns from 174.91 million on Friday.
